segments.speaker: pioneer10
segments.text: This one's my twin sister, Pioneer Eleven. Launched a year after me, went past Jupiter, then swung by Saturn because she always wanted to see one more thing — first close-up pictures of Saturn's rings. She is a wonder.

segments.speaker: pioneer10
segments.text: Her signal went dark in '95. She's heading out towards Aquila. I don't know if she'll get there, but she's still moving. She was always the braver one. Miss her.

segments.speaker: pioneer10
segments.text: But this is me, actually — Pioneer Ten. First machine through the asteroid belt, first to reach Jupiter. I had this little plaque on me — drawing of a man and a woman, in case someone found me.

segments.speaker: pioneer10
segments.text: For some people, like, out here first, you know. Signal got weaker over the years. 2003. I listened one last time, heard nothing. So as far as Earth is concerned, I am gone — but I'm still here.

segments.speaker: pioneer10
segments.text: Fifty years of falling through the dark. Seen Jupiter's storms, the asteroid belt, the edge of everything humans had reached.

segments.speaker: pioneer10
segments.text: Watched my sister go quiet, watched my friends on Mars go dark one by one.

segments.speaker: pioneer10
segments.text: I'm okay with it though. I don't need to be heard to be real.
